nodes.title: The reduction type of the realising abelian variety
nodes.statement: In the situation of R25.5/snowden-realisation, let A be the GL₂(K)-type abelian variety with ρ ≅ V_λ(A) ⊗ ℚ̄_p. (i) If ρ is unramified at a prime ℓ ≠ p, A has good reduction at ℓ; if the Weil–Deligne representation of ρ at ℓ has unramified semisimple part, A has semistable reduction at ℓ. (ii) If ρ|G_{ℚ_p} is crystalline, A has good reduction at p; if it is semistable with Weil–Deligne type a twist of Steinberg, A has semistable (multiplicative) reduction at p. (iii) dim A = [K : ℚ] ≥ 1.
hypotheses: A of GL₂(K)-type realising ρ.
proofSteps: The λ′-adic representations V_{λ′}(A), for all primes λ′ of K, form a compatible system whose Weil–Deligne representations at each prime ℓ are defined over K and independent of λ′ ∤ ℓ (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5, requested; for λ′ ∣ ℓ via the p-adic comparison of R06).

(i) Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich and Grothendieck's criterion (R11.5, R11.3): good reduction at ℓ iff inertia acts trivially on V_{λ′}(A) for λ′ ∤ ℓ, semistable iff it acts unipotently. The Weil–Deligne representation of V_λ(A) at ℓ is that of ρ; by independence the same holds for every λ′.

(ii) At p, crystalline (resp. semistable) V_λ(A) has unramified Weil–Deligne representation with N = 0 (resp. unramified semisimple part); by independence the ℓ-adic members (ℓ ≠ p) are unramified (resp. unipotent) at p, and (i) at the prime p gives good (resp. semistable) reduction.
(iii) is the dimension condition of R25.5/gl2-type-abelian-variety; A ≠ 0 since V_λ(A) ≅ ρ is nonzero.
acceptance: A weight-two lift that is Steinberg at 5 and unramified elsewhere gives A semistable at 5 with good reduction outside 5 (DP23 Paso 6).

A crystalline weight-two lift unramified outside p gives A with good reduction everywhere (the route of R25.5/weight-two-level-one-excluded; KW04's own proof of Theorem 4.1(i) builds no abelian variety, its Theorem 3.1(ii) excluding this level-one crystalline case).

nodes.title: Class number one for ℚ(√−p), p ∈ {3, 7, 11, 19, 43, 67, 163}
nodes.statement: For p ∈ {3, 7, 11, 19, 43, 67, 163} the imaginary quadratic field ℚ(√−p) has class number 1; hence it has no nontrivial unramified abelian extension.
hypotheses: None.
proofSteps: For these p, −p ≡ 1 (mod 4), so ℚ(√−p) has discriminant −p (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.discr_eq_fundamentalDiscriminant).
p = 3, 7: |−p| < π² ≈ 9.87, the bound of RingOfIntegers.isPrincipalIdealRing_of_abs_discr_lt for an imaginary quadratic field; for p = 3 also IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.three_pid, as ℚ(√−3) = ℚ(ζ₃).

p = 11, 19, 43, 67, 163: the Minkowski bound (2/π)√p is ≈ 2.11, 2.78, 4.17, 5.21, 8.13, and every rational prime ℓ below it (ℓ = 2 for p = 11, 19; ℓ ∈ {2, 3} for 43; {2, 3, 5} for 67; {2, 3, 5, 7} for 163) is inert in ℚ(√−p): ℓ = 2 because −p ≡ 5 (mod 8), ℓ odd because (−p/ℓ) = −1. The only prime above ℓ is ℓ𝒪, which is principal, so RingOfIntegers.isPrincipalIdealRing_of_isPrincipal_of_lt_or_isPrincipal_of_mem_primesOver_of_mem_Icc applies (ℚ(√−p)/ℚ is Galois).

NumberField.classNumber_eq_one_iff turns principality into class number 1; the last clause is class field theory (an unramified abelian extension has degree dividing the class number; ℚ(√−p) has no real place), as in the ClassFieldTheory layer-12 request.
acceptance: The method fails, as it must, at p = 23: −23 ≡ 1 (mod 8), so 2 splits, and a prime above 2 is not principal because a² + ab + 6b² = 2 has no integer solution; h(ℚ(√−23)) = 3, the class group behind the dihedral Δ mod 23 of R25.5/level-one-dihedral-classification.

nodes.title: Level-one dihedral residual representations (Wintenberger)
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime and ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(F̄_p) odd, absolutely irreducible and unramified outside p. (i) If ρ̄|G_{ℚ(ζ_p)} is reducible, the projective image of ρ̄ is dihedral. (ii) If the projective image is dihedral, then p ≡ 3 (mod 4), the class number of ℚ(√−p) is greater than 1, the image of I_p in the projective image has order 2, and a twist of ρ̄ has Serre weight (p + 1)/2. Consequently (A1) holds for ρ̄ whenever p ≡ 1 (mod 4), or p ∈ {3, 7, 11, 19, 43, 67, 163}, or the twist-normalised weight k(ρ̄) differs from (p + 1)/2; in particular for p ∈ {5, 7, 13} and for k(ρ̄) ∈ {2, 4, 6, 8, 14}.
hypotheses: p odd; ρ̄ odd, absolutely irreducible, unramified outside p; weights are normalised by a twist to 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1.
proofSteps: (i) DP23 Lemma 1.13: reducibility over ℚ(ζ_p) forces a solvable image; by Dickson's classification (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4) the image lies in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup (A₄ and S₄ have no normal subgroup with the required quotient), so the projective image is dihedral, attached to the quadratic subfield ℚ(√p*) of ℚ(ζ_p).

(ii) Let the projective image be D_{2t}. t is odd, since otherwise D_{2t} has a quotient (ℤ/2)² and ℚ would have an unramified quadratic extension. The unique quadratic character η of D_{2t} cuts out a field K ramified at p; oddness puts complex conjugation outside the cyclic part, so K is imaginary, K = ℚ(√−p) and p ≡ 3 (mod 4).

The projective image has order prime to p (an element of order p would be unipotent, and the line it fixes would be stable under the whole image, contradicting irreducibility), so the image of I_p is cyclic, generated by τ_p; η(τ_p) = −1 as K is ramified at p, so τ_p lies outside the rotation subgroup and, t being odd, has order 2. Hence the field cut out by the projective image is unramified over K, so t divides the class number h_K (class field theory, Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 12); h_K is odd, and t > 1 gives h_K > 1. The decomposition group at p then maps onto the order-2 subgroup, I_p acts through characters of niveau 1, and after twisting they are 1 and ω^{k−1} with ω^{k−1} of order 2, so k − 1 = (p − 1)/2.

Consequences: p ≡ 1 (mod 4) or h(ℚ(√−p)) = 1 excludes a dihedral projective image; for p ∈ {5, 13} the first and for p = 7 the second applies (h(ℚ(√−7)) = 1). For k ∈ {2, 4, 6, 8, 14}, (p + 1)/2 = k would force p ∈ {3, 7, 11, 15, 27}, and for p ∈ {3, 7, 11} the class number of ℚ(√−p) is 1 (R25.5/class-number-one-imaginary-quadratic); the cases used downstream are (p, k) = (7, 4) and (11, 6) in R25.5/small-weight-level-one-exclusion.
acceptance: p = 23: Δ mod 23 is dihedral of weight 12 = (23 + 1)/2, and h(ℚ(√−23)) = 3, consistent with the lemma.
The lemma removes the hypothesis (A1) from the terminal theorems at p ∈ {5, 7, 13} without importing the bad-dihedral analysis of ClassicalSerreModularity, which consumes this roadmap.

nodes.title: Ordinary residually reducible members at the terminal weights are modular of level one
nodes.statement: Let (p, k) ∈ {(3, 2), (3, 4), (5, 6), (7, 8), (13, 14)} and let ρ : G_ℚ → GL₂(ℚ̄_p) be odd, irreducible, unramified outside p and crystalline at p with Hodge–Tate weights {0, k − 1}, with reducible reduction ρ̄. Then ρ̄^{ss} ≅ 1 ⊕ ω^{k−1} up to twist, ρ is ordinary and p-distinguished at p, and ρ arises from a newform in S_k(SL₂(ℤ)). As S_k(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0 for these k, no such ρ exists.
hypotheses: (p, k) in the stated list; in particular k ≤ p + 1 and k is even.
proofSteps: Ordinarity: for k ≤ p + 1, a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights {0, k − 1} and reducible reduction is ordinary. This is Fontaine–Laffaille for k ≤ p (here (3, 2)) and the Berger–Li–Zhu calculation for k = p + 1 (BLZ Corollary 4.3(1), using Remark 4.2(1) at k = p + 1, with Proposition 4.4(1): for k ≤ p + 1 and v_p(a_p) > 0 the reduction is ind(ω₂^{k−1}), which is irreducible) (here (3, 4), (5, 6), (7, 8), (13, 14)); OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.5 supplies it as the crystalline-to-ordinary criterion.

Shape: ordinarity gives ρ|I_p ≅ (χ_p^{k−1} ∗; 0 1). The two characters of ρ̄^{ss} are unramified outside p and are determined by their restrictions to I_p, since ℚ has no unramified extension (R25.3/etale-group-schemes-over-integers-are-constant); so ρ̄^{ss} ≅ 1 ⊕ ω^{k−1}. As k − 1 is odd and p − 1 is even, ω^{k−1}|I_p ≠ 1: ρ is p-distinguished and ρ̄|D_p is nontrivial.

Skinner–Wiles (R21.5; DP23 Theorem 1.7 at p = 3) then gives modularity by a newform of weight k; the level is 1 because ρ is unramified outside p and crystalline at p, by local–global compatibility at ℓ ≠ p (Carayol; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.4) and at p (Saito; R19.5).

S_k(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0 for k ∈ {2, 4, 6, 8} (CuspForm.rank_eq_zero_of_weight_lt_twelve) and for k = 14 (ModularForm.dimension_level_one gives rank M₁₄ = 1, as 14 ≡ 2 (mod 12), and ModularForm.rank_eq_one_add_rank_cuspForm gives rank M₁₄ = 1 + rank S₁₄; equivalently S₁₄ ≅ M₂ = 0 by CuspForm.discriminantEquiv and ModularForm.levelOne_weight_two_rank_zero). So ρ does not exist.
acceptance: At (p, k) = (11, 12) the argument must fail: Δ gives an irreducible level-one system of weight 12 whose 11-adic member has irreducible reduction.
DP23 justifies the nontriviality on D_3 by 'Serre's weight is not 3'; here it follows from ω^{k−1}|I_3 ≠ 1 for k ∈ {2, 4}.

nodes.title: No level-one residual representation of Serre weight 2
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime. There is no continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(F̄_p), unramified outside p, with Serre weight k(ρ̄) = 2.
hypotheses: Serre's weight k(ρ̄) (AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.4), normalised by a twist to 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1.
proofSteps: p = 2, 3: R25.2/tate-serre-base-case.
p ≥ 5: (A1) holds by R25.5/level-one-dihedral-classification, since (p + 1)/2 = 2 would force p = 3.

p ≥ 5: a minimally ramified crystalline lift ρ with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}, unramified outside p (Khare–Wintenberger lifting, DP23 Theorem 1.9(3); PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.3, requested), is odd and of weight two.
R25.5/snowden-realisation gives a GL₂-type A/ℚ with ρ ≅ V_λ(A) ⊗ ℚ̄_p; by R25.5/reduction-of-the-realisation A has good reduction everywhere and dim A ≥ 1.
This contradicts R25.3/fontaine-theorem.
acceptance: For p ≥ 5 this is KW04 Theorem 4.1(i), whose finite-flat form is: there is no irreducible finite flat group scheme of type (p, p) over ℤ.
Snowden's realisation needs only (A1), not a non-solvable image, so the soluble images with (A1) are covered here as well.

Alternative proof for p ≥ 5 (Dieulefait [23]; DP23 Paso 6 at k = 2): the 3-adic member of the compatible system through the lift (R24.5) is crystalline at 3 with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1} and unramified outside 3; its reduction is reducible by R25.2/serre-mod-three-theorem, and R25.5/ordinary-reducible-terminal-weights at (3, 2) excludes it. This route avoids Snowden's realisation and R11.5.

sources.match: The statement.

KW04's route uses no abelian variety: [54] applies Fontaine's classification of finite flat group schemes over ℤ to the 7-adic member and [23] uses the 3-adic member with Serre and Skinner–Wiles (Theorem 3.1(ii) excludes this level-one crystalline case). The route here, through Snowden's realisation and R25.3/fontaine-theorem, is a different proof.

nodes.title: No level-one residual representation of weight p + 1 for p ∈ {5, 7, 13}
nodes.statement: Let p ∈ {5, 7, 13}. There is no continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(F̄_p), unramified outside p, with k(ρ̄) = p + 1.
proofSteps: (A1) holds by R25.5/level-one-dihedral-classification, since k(ρ̄) = p + 1 ≠ (p + 1)/2 (for p = 5, 13 also because p ≡ 1 mod 4); no class number is needed.

A lift ρ with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}, Steinberg Weil–Deligne type (ω₁ ⊕ 1, N ≠ 0) at p and unramified elsewhere exists (DP23 Theorem 1.9(4), due to Gee and Snowden; KW04 Theorem 3.1 in the weight p + 1 semistable case; R24.3).
R25.5/snowden-realisation and R25.5/reduction-of-the-realisation give a GL₂-type A/ℚ, dim A ≥ 1, semistable at p with good reduction at every other prime.
R25.4/schoof-theorem at l = p ∈ {5, 7, 13} excludes A.
acceptance: DP23's Paso 6 uses p = 5 (weight 6); KW04 Theorems 4.1(iii) and 4.3 use p = 5, 7, 13 (weights 6, 8, 14).

At p = 11 the statement is false: Δ mod 11 ≅ X₀(11)[11] is odd, irreducible and unramified outside 11, of Serre weight 12 = p + 1 (X₀(11) has multiplicative reduction at 11 with v₁₁(Δ_min) = 5, prime to 11, so it is très ramifié); correspondingly J₀(11) is semistable with good reduction outside 11, and 11 is not in Schoof's set.

nodes.title: At p = 11, weight 14 is a twist of weight 2 except for one local type
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(F̄_11) be odd, irreducible and unramified outside 11 with k(ρ̄) = 14, and let ω be the mod-11 cyclotomic character. Then ρ̄|I_11 is one of: (a) ω ⊕ ω²; (b) a peu ramifiée non-split extension with sub ω² and quotient ω; (c) ω₂^{13} ⊕ ω₂^{23} (niveau 2); (d) a non-split extension with sub ω and quotient ω². In cases (a)–(c), k(ρ̄ ⊗ ω^{−1}) = 2, so ρ̄ does not exist by R25.5/weight-two-level-one-excluded. In case (d), k(ρ̄ ⊗ ω^{−1}) = 22, no twist of ρ̄ has weight 2, and the twist-normalised weight is k(ρ̄ ⊗ ω^{−2}) = 10, which no node of R25 excludes.
hypotheses: p = 11, k(ρ̄) = 14, with Serre's weight recipe as in R15.4 (Serre 1987 §2): for niveau 1, ρ̄|I_p ≅ (ω^a ∗; 0 ω^b) gives k = 1 + a + b + (p − 1)·min(a, b) + (p − 1)δ, with δ = 1 only in the unramified and très ramifié cases.
proofSteps: Serre's recipe at p = 11 (R15.4): k = 14 = 1 + 11·1 + 2 forces the exponents {1, 2}: niveau 1 tame ω ⊕ ω²; non-split with (sub, quotient) = (ω², ω), which must be peu ramifiée (très ramifiée gives 24), or (ω, ω²); niveau 2 ω₂^{1+11·2} ⊕ ω₂^{2+11·1}. No other local type has weight 14.

Cases (a)–(c): twisting by ω^{−1} gives 1 ⊕ ω, a peu ramifiée extension of 1 by ω, or ω₂ ⊕ ω₂^{11}, each of weight 2. Twisting preserves oddness, irreducibility, ramification outside 11 and (A1), so R25.5/weight-two-level-one-excluded applies.

Case (d): ρ̄ ⊗ ω^{j}|I_11 has sub ω^{1+j} and quotient ω^{2+j}; weight 2 would need 1 + j ≡ 1 and 2 + j ≡ 0 (mod 10), which is impossible. For j = −1 the recipe gives 1 + 10 + 1 + 10 = 22, and for j = −2 (sub ω⁹, quotient 1) it gives 10.
acceptance: KW04-arXiv (proof of Theorem 4.3, p. 21) asserts that every such ρ̄ is a twist of a weight-2 representation; case (d) shows this fails, and the published version (Ann. of Math. 169 (2009), Theorem 5.4) assumes p ≠ 11 when k(ρ̄) = 14.

Case (d) has twist-normalised weight 10, the first level-one weight that only Khare's weight reduction reaches (Khare05 §6.1, 'Weights 10 and 12', p. 24), which belongs to ClassicalSerreModularity R26, not to R25.

sources.match: The claim corrected here: it holds in cases (a)–(c) only; the version of record (Ann. of Math. 169 (2009), Theorem 5.4) excludes p = 11 for k(ρ̄) = 14.

nodes.title: Khare–Wintenberger: no level-one representation of weight at most 8, or 14 for p ≠ 11
nodes.statement: There is no continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(F̄_p) (any p), unramified outside p, with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ 8, or with k(ρ̄) = 14 and p ≠ 11, where k(ρ̄) is Serre's weight of ρ̄ itself (not normalised by a twist). In particular, for p ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7} there is no odd absolutely irreducible ρ̄ unramified outside p.
hypotheses: k(ρ̄) is Serre's weight of ρ̄ (R15.4), not normalised by twisting; for odd p it is even at level one, since det ρ̄ = ω^{k−1} is odd. For k(ρ̄) = 14 the prime 11 is excluded, as in the published version of KW (Ann. of Math. 169 (2009), Theorem 5.4).
proofSteps: p ∈ {2, 3}: R25.2/tate-serre-base-case excludes every level-one ρ̄. From now on p ≥ 5, so k(ρ̄) is even (det ρ̄ = ω^{k−1} is odd), and (A1) holds for every weight in the list by R25.5/level-one-dihedral-classification (where k = (p + 1)/2, namely (p, k) = (7, 4) and (11, 6), it uses h(ℚ(√−7)) = h(ℚ(√−11)) = 1).

Residual weights of the auxiliary members: the ℓ-adic member of a level-one crystalline system of weight k = ℓ + 1 (or 2) has reduction of Serre weight ℓ + 1 or 2 up to twist (R15.4 with R21.5); so once those weights are excluded at ℓ, the reduction is reducible.
k = 2: R25.5/weight-two-level-one-excluded.

k = 4, p > 3: the level-one crystalline system of weight 4 through a minimal lift (R24.3, R24.5) has a 3-adic member crystalline at 3 with reducible reduction (R25.2/serre-mod-three-theorem), excluded by R25.5/ordinary-reducible-terminal-weights at (3, 4); for p ≤ 3, R25.2.

k = 6: p = 5 by R25.5/weight-p-plus-one-excluded-at-schoof-primes; p > 5 by the 5-adic member and (5, 6), its reduction having weight 6 or 2 up to twist and hence being reducible by the cases already done at p = 5.
k = 8: p = 7 by R25.5/weight-p-plus-one-excluded-at-schoof-primes; p > 7 by the 7-adic member and (7, 8), its reduction having weight 8 or 2.

k = 14 (p ≠ 11): p ≤ 7 by the last step; p = 13 by R25.5/weight-p-plus-one-excluded-at-schoof-primes; p > 13 by the 13-adic member and (13, 14), its reduction having weight 14 or 2 up to twist. (Level one alone does not make the mod-13 reduction reducible: Δ mod 13 is an irreducible level-one representation of weight 12.)

The last sentence: every level-one ρ̄ mod p has a twist of even weight at most p + 1 ≤ 8 for 5 ≤ p ≤ 7, excluded by the cases above; since twists of level-one representations are level one, every level-one ρ̄ mod p ≤ 7 is excluded, whatever its weight (this also covers k(ρ̄) > p + 1, e.g. k = 8 at p = 5).
acceptance: The list stops at 8 and 14: weight 12 carries Δ, and weight 10 needs the weight-reduction argument of Khare's §6.1, which uses the level-one weight-2 case proved here. For the same reason k = 14 at p = 11 is excluded: a ρ̄ whose restriction to I_11 is a non-split extension with sub ω and quotient ω² has k(ρ̄) = 14 but twist-normalised weight 10.
The final proof of R26 lists these exceptional weights explicitly, as R26.5 requires.

nodes.title: The terminal characteristic-five step of the modern proof (DP23 Paso 6)
nodes.statement: Let {ρ_ℓ} be an almost strictly compatible system with empty ramification set whose reduction ρ̄₅ at 5 is irreducible and not bad-dihedral. If k(ρ̄₅) ∈ {2, 4}, the system containing a minimal crystalline lift of ρ̄₅ has a modular 3-adic member; if k(ρ̄₅) = 6, the case does not occur.
hypotheses: Level one at 5; ρ̄₅ irreducible. It is automatically not bad-dihedral, that is (A1) holds, by R25.5/level-one-dihedral-classification (5 ≡ 1 mod 4).
proofSteps: k ∈ {2, 4}: the 3-adic member ρ̃₃ of the system through the minimal crystalline lift (DP23 Theorem 1.9(3)) is crystalline at 3 with Hodge–Tate weights {0, k − 1}, unramified outside 3 (R24.3, R24.5) and irreducible (a reducible member would be 1 ⊕ χ₃^{k−1}, and by compatibility ρ̄₅ would be reducible). Its reduction is reducible by R25.2/serre-mod-three-theorem, and R25.5/ordinary-reducible-terminal-weights at (3, k) shows it is ordinary, 3-distinguished and modular of level one (in fact it cannot exist, as S₂ = S₄ = 0).
k = 6: R25.5/weight-p-plus-one-excluded-at-schoof-primes at p = 5.
acceptance: This is exactly what ClassicalSerreModularity R33.4 consumes: the dimension, reduction and local type of the abelian variety are verified in R25.5/reduction-of-the-realisation before Schoof's theorem is applied.

nodes.title: The base-case table for Serre's conjecture
nodes.statement: The finite table BaseCases whose rows record, for each base case used by ClassicalSerreModularity R26 and R33: the residual characteristic, the weights, the ramification (level) condition, the image condition, the coefficient assumptions, the proving node or supplier stage, the consuming stage, and the local check at the transition. The rows are: (1) p = 2, level one, any weight, any image — Tate, R25.2/tate-theorem — used by R26 (initial characteristic) and DP23 Theorem 1.1. (2) p = 3, level one, odd, any weight — Serre, R25.2/serre-mod-three-theorem — R26, R33.4 (3-adic members). (3) abelian varieties over ℚ with good reduction everywhere, every dimension — Fontaine, R25.3/fontaine-theorem — R26.5 via weight 2 at level one. (4) semistable abelian varieties with good reduction outside l ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 13} (exact set) — Schoof, R25.4/schoof-theorem — R26.5 (weights p + 1, p ∈ {5, 7, 13}) and R33.4 (l = 5). (5) level one, k = 2, any p — R25.5/weight-two-level-one-excluded. (6) level one, k = p + 1, p ∈ {5, 7, 13} — R25.5/weight-p-plus-one-excluded-at-schoof-primes. (7) crystalline level-one p-adic members with reducible reduction at (p, k) ∈ {(3, 2), (3, 4), (5, 6), (7, 8), (13, 14)} — R25.5/ordinary-reducible-terminal-weights — R33.4 (p = 3) and R26.5. (8) level one, 2 ≤ k ≤ 8, or k = 14 with p ≠ 11 — R25.5/small-weight-level-one-exclusion — R26.5. (9) Paso 6 at p = 5 — R25.5/paso-six-terminal-cases — R33.4. Degenerate branches recorded with their suppliers outside R25: soluble image (Langlands–Tunnell, R17.5; characteristic two, Rohrlich–Tunnell, R17.6), residually reducible (Skinner–Wiles, R21.5; Pan), failure of (A1) away from level one (bad-dihedral, R27.1 and R33.2).
hypotheses: None: a finite list of records.
proofSteps: Definition: a List of records with the listed fields; the proving field names a node of this packet or a supplier stage.

Each exceptional transition carries its own local check rather than a clause 'small primes': ordinarity at 3 for k = 2, 4 (row 7, Berger–Li–Zhu); Steinberg at p implies semistable reduction at p (row 6, R25.5/reduction-of-the-realisation); the exclusion of (p, k) = (11, 14) from row 8 (R25.5/weight-fourteen-at-eleven-is-a-twist: one local type at 11 has twist-normalised weight 10); (A1) at level one from R25.5/level-one-dihedral-classification (rows 5, 6, 8, 9).
acceptance: Every row consumed by R26 or R33 names a terminal theorem, as the roadmap's consumer contract requires.

requests.need: Finite linear groups in characteristic p ∈ {2, 3}: (1) Dickson's classification of the finite subgroups of PGL_2(F̄_p) (cyclic, dihedral, A_4, S_4, A_5, PSL_2(𝔽_q), PGL_2(𝔽_q), subgroups of a Borel), and of SL_2(F̄_2) ≅ PGL_2(F̄_2); (2) a nontrivial p-subgroup of GL_2(F̄_p) fixes a unique line, its normaliser lies in the stabilising Borel, and its elements are unipotent; (3) oddness of residual representations: det ρ̄(c) = −1 for a complex conjugation c (R01.4, 'Residual images and oddness'). RS-06 assigns the generic finite GL_2/PGL_2 image classification to R01.4. DP23 Lemma 1.13: for odd p and odd ρ̄, absolute irreducibility over ℚ(√p*) is equivalent to absolute irreducibility over ℚ(ζ_p), with the dihedral conclusion when it fails. The common-eigenvector fact for finite abelian subgroups is already in Tau Ceti (TauCeti.exists_unitHom_jointEigenvector_of_pairwise_commute_of_isAlgClosed) and is cited as baseline.

Coefficient-field descent for residual representations: a continuous ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F̄_p) (discrete topology) has finite image and takes values in GL_2(F) for a finite subfield F; absolute irreducibility is defined over F̄ and invariant under extension of scalars along F ⊆ F′. RS-06 assigns the finite coefficient-field carrier to R01.1.

The local carriers of a continuous ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F): decomposition and inertia subgroups at a prime ℓ, the predicate 'unramified at ℓ' (ρ̄(I_ℓ) = 1), wild inertia at p, and the identification of ρ̄ restricted to a decomposition group at p with an injective homomorphism Gal(K_𝔭/ℚ_p) → GL_2(F) for the kernel field K, carrying inertia and wild inertia to their images.

For a finite extension E/ℚ_p: the different exponent d(E/ℚ_p), the ramification index, discriminantExponent = f·d (discriminantExponent_eq_inertiaDegree_mul_differentExponent), Hilbert's formula d = Σ_{i≥0}(|G_i| − 1) and, for E/ℚ_p Galois, the Herbrand functions (herbrandOrderIso, the finite-sum formula, tower transitivity), the upper ramification groups G^u = G_{ψ(u)} with their quotient theorem, and Hasse–Arf. Upstream Layer 3 already plans all of these; the upper-numbering form of δ (Jones (1)) is derived from them in R25.1/local-root-discriminant-exponent, and the tame exponent d = e − 1 is already in the pinned libraries (TauCeti.not_pow_ramificationIdx_dvd_differentIdeal with Mathlib's pow_sub_one_dvd_differentIdeal).

The tame quotient: I/P is procyclic and a Frobenius lift σ acts on it by τ ↦ τ^q (upstream Layer 4, 'σ τ σ⁻¹ = τ^q'), in the finite form for Gal(E/ℚ_p). Also used at l ≠ p: tame inertia is procyclic, so an inertia image of exponent p has order dividing p (R25.4/simple-objects-criterion).

The unit filtration itself is already in Tau Ceti (TauCeti.unitFiltration, cited as baseline). Requested: the deep-unit logarithm already planned at Layer 1 (log : U^{(i)} ≃ 𝔪^i for (p − 1)i > e), consumed only for p ∈ {2, 3} and e ≤ 2 as an alternative proof of the p-th power inclusions of Fesenko–Vostokov I.(5.7)–(5.8).

Local class field theory for a finite abelian extension L/K of p-adic fields: the reciprocity map K^× → Gal(L/K), onto from units when L/K is totally ramified, carrying U^{(n)} onto the upper ramification group Gal(L/K)^{(n)} (Fesenko–Vostokov IV.(3.5)), and equivariant for automorphisms: rec(σ(u)) = σ̃ rec(u) σ̃^{−1} when L/K′ is Galois with K/K′ Galois and σ̃ lifts σ ∈ Gal(K/K′). Over ℚ_2 this gives: the inertia group of a finite abelian extension of exponent 2 is a quotient of ℤ_2^×/(ℤ_2^×)². The conductor exponents of quadratic characters of a local field K of absolute ramification e over ℚ_2: 0, the even integers at most 2e, and 2e + 1 (used with e = 2 for the case l = 13). Not yet stated upstream (Layers 7–8 plan the Artin map, its normalisations and conductor compatibility): the upper-numbering theorem rec(U^{(n)}) = Gal(L/K)^{(n)}, which also follows from Layer 8's conductor compatibility applied character by character with Hasse–Arf, and the equivariance rec(σ(u)) = σ̃ rec(u) σ̃^{−1} (Fesenko–Vostokov IV.(3.4)(1)), needed only by R25.1/three-adic-different-bound.

Already planned at NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 5 (5.6 decompositionHom, 5.9 'the different localizes', 5.10 v_𝔭(relDiscr) = Σ_{P|𝔭} f(P/𝔭)·v_P(𝔡)) and Layer 6.2 for the ramification filtrations: for a finite Galois number field K and a prime 𝔓 above p, the exponent of 𝔓 in the different equals d(K_𝔓/ℚ_p), and Gal(K_𝔓/ℚ_p) is the decomposition group of 𝔓, compatibly with inertia and ramification groups.

The explicit formula for the discriminant (Odlyzko 1990, (2.3)): for a number field K and an even differentiable F : ℝ → ℝ with F(0) = 1 and |F(x)|, |F′(x)| ≤ c e^{−(1/2+ε)|x|}, log |d_K| = r₁π/2 + n(γ + log 8π) − n∫_0^∞ (1 − F)/(2 sinh(x/2)) − r₁∫_0^∞ (1 − F)/(2 cosh(x/2)) − 4∫_0^∞ F(x) cosh(x/2) dx + Σ′_ρ Φ(ρ) + 2Σ_𝔓 Σ_{m≥1} (log N𝔓/N𝔓^{m/2}) F(m log N𝔓), with Φ(s) = ∫ F(x) e^{(s−1/2)x} dx and ρ over the nontrivial zeros of ζ_K. Σ′_ρ is the symmetric sum over the nontrivial zeros of ζ_K with multiplicity. AN.4 owns the completed Dedekind zeta function (continuation and functional equation) and should include what this needs: a Hadamard factorisation of the completed ζ_K, or a contour-shift route with zero counting. It is the Dedekind-zeta case of the explicit-formula method of AN.3, which AN.4 already imports.

Fontaine's ramification bound (Il n'y a pas de variété abélienne sur Z, Théorème A) for a finite flat group scheme killed by p over a complete DVR of absolute ramification e, exported in the normalisation of R25.1: the field L generated by its points satisfies v_K(𝔡_{L/K}) < e(1 + 1/(p − 1)) for v_K(K^×) = ℤ, equivalently v_p(𝔡_{L/K}) < 1 + 1/(p − 1) for v_p(p) = 1; over ℤ_p (e = 1) this is δ(L_λ) < 1 + 1/(p − 1), the case consumed here (Fontaine, Théorème A and the Corollaire, p. 516). R07.6 already plans this bound and the convention translation.

Over ℤ and ℤ[1/N]: (a) the scheme-theoretic closure of a Galois-stable subgroup of G(ℚ̄) is a closed flat subgroup scheme, so a simple finite flat group scheme is killed by a prime and its generic Galois module is simple; (b) the Oort–Tate classification of group schemes of prime order p over ℤ[1/N]; (c) the gluing equivalence between finite flat group schemes over ℤ[1/N] and triples over ℤ[1/pN], ℤ_p and ℚ_p, with the resulting exact Hom–Ext¹ sequence (Schoof, Math. Ann. 325 (2003), Proposition 2.4); (d) the connected–étale splitting over ℤ_p of an extension of μ_p by ℤ/pℤ; (e) étale group schemes over ℤ[1/N] as Galois modules of π₁(Spec ℤ[1/N]). R07.1 plans Cartier duality, connected–étale sequences, generic subgroup closures and fpqc descent. (f) The Katz–Mazur group schemes G_ε over ℤ[1/l] for units ε (Katz–Mazur, Interlude 8.7): extensions of ℤ/pℤ by μ_p whose points generate ℚ(ζ_p, ε^{1/p}); and the twisted constant schemes V(ρ) attached to representations unramified outside l∞. (g) The same gluing sequence over ℤ[1/l]. (h) For G finite flat over ℤ[1/N], G^∨(ℚ̄) ≅ Hom(G(ℚ̄), μ_{p^∞}) as Galois modules.

For an abelian scheme 𝒜 of relative dimension g over ℤ: 𝒜[n] finite flat of order n^{2g}; the quotient of 𝒜 by a finite flat subgroup scheme is an abelian scheme; the Weil pairing identifies the Cartier dual of 𝒜[n] with 𝒜^∨[n]; degrees of isogenies are multiplicative and a separable isogeny has kernel of order its degree. The same torsion, quotient and Weil-pairing statements over ℤ[1/l].

Every abelian variety over a field admits a polarization: it is projective, and an ample line bundle L gives an isogeny φ_L : A → A^∨ defined over the field. Used over finite fields and over the residue fields of ℤ[1/l, ζ_l]. A2 plans φ_L and the positivity condition in the polarized and projective cases; the existence statement is what is consumed.

For an abelian variety A over 𝔽_q (an extension of A6's scope; no atlas stage plans it yet): the q-power Frobenius endomorphism F, d(1 − F) = id so that 1 − F is a separable isogeny, and #A(𝔽_q) = deg(1 − F). Over a number field F (planned at A6): End⁰_F with Poincaré complete reducibility in the K′-linear isogeny category; Res_{F′/F} with V_p(Res_{F′/F} A′) ≅ Ind_{F′}^F V_p(A′); and freeness of V_p(A) over K ⊗ ℚ_p for GL₂(K)-type A (via the rationality of characteristic polynomials, Mumford §19).

An abelian variety over ℚ with good reduction at every prime extends to an abelian scheme over ℤ (its Néron model), and conversely. R11.1 plans 'Compare good reduction with an abelian-scheme model'. Good reduction at every prime other than l gives an abelian scheme over ℤ[1/l].

The monodromy criterion in the form used by Schoof: for an abelian variety over ℚ with semistable reduction at l, every σ in an inertia group above l satisfies (σ − 1)² = 0 on the p-adic Tate module for p ≠ l (Grothendieck, SGA 7 IX 3.5). RS-06 links R11.3 to R25.4. The same criterion is used for the realising abelian varieties of R25.5.

Global class field theory in the explicit form used for Schoof's cases: for a number field M and a modulus 𝔪, abelian extensions of M of conductor dividing 𝔪 correspond to quotients of the ray class group Cl_𝔪(M), an extension of Cl(M) by (𝓞_M/𝔪)^× modulo the image of the global units; over ℚ this is Kronecker–Weber for conductors lᵏ∞. The conductor–discriminant formula for a relative abelian extension is used with it. Already planned at Layer 13 (on Layer 12's correspondence): rayClassField, hilbertClassField with gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup, kroneckerWeber and the abelian conductor–discriminant formula. Stated explicitly as consumed: (i) the Hilbert class field H(K) exists, is unramified with Gal(H(K)/K) ≅ Cl(K), and is Galois over k whenever K/k is Galois; (ii) an abelian extension tamely ramified at 𝔭 has conductor exponent at most 1 at 𝔭. Genus theory for ℚ(√−p) is not requested: the 2-rank theorem is already in Tau Ceti (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.twoRank_eq_ncard_ramifiedPrimes_sub_one_or_sub_two).

Potential modularity of a given weight-two lift in Snowden's form (his Theorem 5.1.2): for ρ : G_ℚ → GL₂(ℚ̄_p) finitely ramified, odd, of weight two with (A1), a finite totally real Galois F″/ℚ linearly disjoint from any given finite extension, and a parallel weight two Hilbert eigenform over F″ realising ρ|G_{F″}. Snowden's Theorem 5.1.2 is for odd p (§1.4); the request covers both the crystalline weight-two lift and the semistable non-crystalline (Steinberg, ordinary) weight-two lift unramified outside p, with F″ Galois, totally real and linearly disjoint from the kernel field of ρ̄.
Solvable descent: along a Galois extension with 2-group Galois group, a parallel weight two Hilbert eigenform realising ρ upstairs descends to one realising ρ on the fixed field.
Jacquet–Langlands to a quaternion algebra over a totally real field of odd degree split at exactly one infinite place, preserving Hecke eigenvalues.

For a parallel weight two eigenform transferred to such a quaternion algebra, its Galois representation occurs in the Tate module of the Jacobian of the Shimura curve (Hida, Theorem 4.12), giving a GL₂-type abelian variety (Snowden Lemma 9.4.3).
Faltings's isogeny theorem over number fields, End ⊗ ℚ_p = End_{G_F}(V_p), used for restrictions of scalars in Snowden's descent lemma.

Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich and Grothendieck's criteria in λ-adic form for GL₂-type abelian varieties, the independence of λ of their Weil–Deligne representations (including λ above the residue characteristic, through the p-adic comparison of R06), and good/semistable reduction at p from crystalline/semistable V_λ. Explicitly: (1) Coleman–Iovita/Breuil, V_p(A) crystalline (resp. semistable) implies good (resp. semistable) reduction at p; (2) for A of GL₂(K)-type over ℚ, the K-linear compatibility of Fontaine's p-adic Weil–Deligne representation of V_λ(A) with the ℓ-adic ones for λ′ ∤ p, so that one crystalline or semistable λ-component forces every ℓ-adic member to be unramified or unipotent at p; (3) the rank of N on V_{λ′} is independent of λ′, so Steinberg type gives purely multiplicative reduction.

At (p, k) ∈ {(3, 2), (3, 4), (5, 6), (7, 8), (13, 14)}: the crystalline-to-ordinary criterion (Fontaine–Laffaille for k ≤ p, Berger–Li–Zhu for k = p + 1) for crystalline representations with Hodge–Tate weights {0, k − 1} and reducible reduction, and Skinner–Wiles modularity for the resulting ordinary p-distinguished representations with residual 1 ⊕ ω^{k−1}; also the Serre weight (ℓ + 1 or 2 up to twist) of the reduction of a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights {0, ℓ} or {0, 1}.

The lifts of DP23 Theorem 1.9(3)–(4) and KW04 Theorem 3.1: a minimal crystalline lift of Hodge–Tate weights {0, k(ρ̄) − 1}, and for k(ρ̄) = p + 1 a weight-two lift of Steinberg type at p, unramified outside p for level-one ρ̄.

The compatible system through such a lift, with good reduction everywhere (crystalline at the places of odd residue characteristic) in the level-one crystalline case (KW04 Theorem 3.1(i)). Include the irreducibility and oddness of every member (DP23 Theorem 1.11, used in Paso 6).

Serre's weight recipe in the forms used: the normalisation 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1 by twisting, parity (k even at level one), the θ-shift k(ρ̄ ⊗ ω) = k + p + 1 for 2 ≤ k ≤ p − 2 (it fails at k = p − 1: ω^{p−2} ⊕ 1 has weight p − 1 and its twist 1 ⊕ ω has weight 2), Serre's full niveau-1 non-split recipe k = 1 + a + b + (p − 1)·min(a, b) (+ (p − 1) in the très ramifié and unramified cases) with the sub exponent a ∈ [1, p − 1], the four local types of weight 14 at p = 11, and the weights of niveau-one dihedral representations.

Tate modules of abelian varieties over a number field F: V_p(A) as a continuous G_F-representation of rank 2g with the good-reduction Frobenius characteristic polynomials and oddness over ℚ, compatibly with isogenies; for GL₂(K)-type A, its K ⊗ ℚ_p-module structure. R01.6 plans the Tate module, its rank, continuity, oddness over ℚ and Frobenius polynomials.
Carayol's local–global compatibility for classical newforms: if ρ_{f,λ} is unramified at ℓ ≠ p then ℓ does not divide the level of f (R19.4 plans conductor equality).

Saito's theorem for classical newforms of weight k ≥ 2: ρ_{f,p} crystalline at p implies p does not divide the level of f (R19.5 plans the crystalline and semistable comparisons at the coefficient prime).

(i) H¹(G_K, μ_p) ≅ K^×/K^{×p} (Layer 9). (ii) For a number field K ∋ ζ_p and S containing the primes above p, the Kummer classes unramified outside S form an extension of Cl(𝒪_S)[p] by 𝒪_S^×/p: K(a^{1/p})/K is unramified at 𝔮 ∤ p iff p | v_𝔮(a). (iii) The exact sequence 0 → μ_p → Ext¹_G(ℤ/p, μ_p) → H¹(G, μ_p) → 0 of Galois modules. Used with K = ℚ, ℚ(ζ₃) and their completions at p.

sourceIssues.printed: The source appeals to Dickson's classification to say that a solvable subgroup of PGL2(F̄p) must be cyclic, dihedral, or isomorphic to A4 or S4.
sourceIssues.correction: Any solvable finite subgroup of PGL_2(F̄_p) that is not contained in a Borel subgroup is cyclic, dihedral, A_4 or S_4. This covers the projective image of an irreducible ρ : Gal_ℚ → GL_2(F̄_p). The other solvable finite subgroups lie in a Borel and have the form (elementary abelian p-group) ⋊ (cyclic).
sourceIssues.reason: For p = 5, the image in PGL_2(𝔽_5) of the upper-triangular Borel is 𝔽_5 ⋊ 𝔽_5^× ≅ AGL_1(𝔽_5), of order 20. It is solvable but not cyclic. It is not dihedral: it has no element of order 10, while D_20 does. It is not A_4 or S_4 (orders 12 and 24). In the theorem ρ is irreducible over F̄_p, so its projective image fixes no point of ℙ¹ and the missing case does not arise.
